meta.title: AI depth proposal: PAI stages, ACS sandboxes, RAG and agent hosting
meta.requirement: 2026-10-31: focus on AI products as much as cloud products; present sandbox environments for model training or agent hosting with ACS sandboxes, and PAI-EAS for post-training and RAG.
meta.basis: Four research areas (pai, sandboxes, rag-agents, patterns) and their fact-checks. Only facts the fact-checks confirmed or corrected are used; unverifiable items are kept out of catalog text and listed under openQuestions.
conventions: catalog[].action 'add' gives a full CatalogEntry. 'change' gives the id plus only the fields to set; each listed field replaces the old value wholesale (pairsWith and alternatives are full lists, not deltas). Unlisted fields stay.
kind 'offering' entries go to offerings.json, 'service' entries to products.json.

Prompt rows show only id, name, scope, lane, rank, purpose, pairs-with and flags; avoidWhen goes to the WHEN NOT TO USE section. useWhen, note, regions and intents never reach the model, so model-facing facts live in purpose, avoidWhen and the new rules.

New PAI stage entries carry no pathRank, like model-studio and pai: they are called by the app or AI Gateway and call stores, and EAS can also host an agent app that calls AI Gateway, so any fixed rank would raise false path-order warnings.
Region ids are limited to the open REGIONS in packages/core/src/regions.ts. Atlanta (us-southeast-1) and Riyadh appear in Alibaba region tables but are not open in regions.ts, so they are left out.

measured.suggestedBudget: 13,500 with R19-R21; 14,000 if the worked example is adopted
measured.note: Measured with estimateTokens (4 chars per token) on a patched in-memory catalog by the synthesizer's validation script, which also checked ids, references, word and length limits, key conflicts, the offerings range, resolution of the new aliases, pattern edges against pathRank, the eval cases with eval/lib.ts checkCases, and the worked example through validateOp, applyOp, repairGraph and checkGraph (no warnings).

testChanges: packages/core/test/prompt.test.ts: the 12,500-token system prompt budget cannot hold these rules and rows; raise it (see meta.measured) or trim elsewhere. This is a cost decision: with implicit caching (96% hit in Phase 0) the extra prefix is mostly cached.
packages/core/test/catalog.test.ts 'resolve: ids from the recorded probe streams': pai_eas now resolves to pai-eas, not pai.
apps/web/scripts/icons/mapping.json: every catalog id needs a mapping row, including the legacy and china-only entries (see icons).
eval/check-cases.ts will reject the new eval cases until the catalog adds the new ids.

entry.name: PAI Elastic Algorithm Service (EAS)
entry.purpose: Managed online serving for your own LLMs, RAG services and agent apps, with autoscaling.
entry.useWhen: Self-hosted or fine-tuned models behind a private endpoint, RAG services, or agent and Dify apps on GPUs.
entry.avoidWhen: Calling hosted Qwen models with no custom weights; use Model Studio. Training; use PAI-DLC.
entry.note: Billed for as long as resources are held, even if a service fails to start. Public pool is pay-as-you-go; dedicated groups are subscription or pay-as-you-go (delete machines to stop billing). Shared gateway by default; ALB or managed dedicated gateways, VPC direct, NLB and Nacos are options. Scale to zero is not allowed with a dedicated gateway. Calling Model Studio or the internet needs NAT with SNAT.
intents: host our own LLM behind a private endpoint
RAG chatbot on a self-hosted model
host an agent or Dify app on GPUs

catalog.rationale: The node customers ask for most (private LLM hosting, RAG, agent and Dify apps, post-training output). It has its own buying options, gateways and network behaviour, so it cannot stay an alias of the pai umbrella. Region scope with vpcAttachable matches it: a managed control plane that places ENIs in the customer vSwitch when a VPC is configured. layout.ts always draws region scope on the shelf, so private access is drawn as an edge (prompt rule R19).

entry.name: PAI Deep Learning Containers (DLC)
entry.purpose: Managed distributed training and fine-tuning jobs on GPU pools or Lingjun quotas, without running clusters.
entry.useWhen: Multi-GPU or multi-node fine-tuning, pre-training or RL jobs that read data from OSS, NAS or CPFS.
entry.avoidWhen: Interactive experiments (use PAI-DSW) or serving a model (use PAI-EAS).
entry.note: Public resources are pay-as-you-go; resource quotas are subscription. Lingjun quotas need allowlist access. Model Gallery fine-tuning jobs run here. The official Megatron and GRPO walkthroughs recommend or require China (Ulanqab); check Singapore capacity first.
intents: fine-tune or post-train a model on our data

catalog.rationale: Training and serving must be separate boxes so a diagram can show train -> checkpoints -> deploy. DLC is where Model Gallery, the Megatron walkthrough and the ChatLearn GRPO guide run multi-node jobs.

entry.name: PAI Data Science Workshop (DSW)
entry.purpose: Cloud notebook, VS Code and terminal workspaces on CPU or GPU for model development.
entry.useWhen: Per-person GPU environments where data scientists prototype, fine-tune and debug before DLC jobs or EAS.
entry.avoidWhen: Production serving or long multi-node training; use PAI-EAS or PAI-DLC.
entry.note: Public resources are pay-as-you-go; dedicated quotas (general or Lingjun) are subscription. Mounts OSS, NAS or CPFS. Attach a RAM role so notebooks use STS credentials instead of AccessKeys. The overview describes no isolation beyond that, so separate teams by workspace or VPC.

catalog.rationale: A customer who asks for 'sandbox environments for model training' usually means per-person dev environments for people. That is DSW, not an agent sandbox. Without this entry the model has no way to tell a notebook from a training job or a serving endpoint.

entry.name: PAI Model Gallery
entry.purpose: Open-model catalog with no-code fine-tuning (SFT, DPO) on DLC and one-click deployment to EAS.
entry.useWhen: Fine-tuning or deploying open models such as Qwen3 without writing training code.
entry.avoidWhen: Custom training code or large pre-training; use PAI-DLC directly.
entry.note: Free itself; you pay for the DLC jobs and EAS services it starts. SFT and DPO with full-parameter, LoRA or QLoRA. GRPO is documented only in the Qwen3 guide, for Qwen3 32B and smaller.
intents: fine-tune an open model on our data without code

catalog.rationale: Post-training is a headline example, and Model Gallery is the documented no-code path. It has no compute of its own but launches DLC jobs and EAS services, so it is drawn as an orchestrating node with control edges. An alias cannot do this, because 'Model Gallery' would have to resolve to both DLC and EAS.

entry.name: Agent Sandbox Container Edition (ACS)
entry.purpose: VM-isolated agent sandboxes as pods in your ACS cluster, with warm pools, hibernation and E2B API.
entry.useWhen: Many agent or RL-rollout sandboxes on Kubernetes with warm pools, multi-tenancy and VPC egress control.
entry.avoidWhen: GPU work inside the sandbox (none), or no Kubernetes; use agent-sandbox for a managed E2B API.
entry.note: Public preview per the ACS page (2026-06-23); confirm with the account team. CPU and memory only, no GPU. Needs Agent Sandbox activated on an ACS cluster, the controller and sandbox-manager add-ons, and an Ingress (ALB) with a domain and TLS. Default creation quota is low (burst 100, then 20 per minute): request more for RL fleets. Sandbox types per region are not listed.
intents: agent sandboxes on our own Kubernetes (ACS)
sandbox fleet for agent RL rollouts
multi-tenant code execution for our agent platform

catalog.rationale: The user's own words are 'ACS sandboxes'. Container Edition sandboxes are pods inside the customer's ACS cluster and VPC, so the entry is VPC-scoped in the compute lane, drawn as an ordinary node with an edge from the acs node (like dify-on-ack from ack). Today the alias 'ACS Agent Sandbox' points at the region-scoped agent-sandbox entry, which would draw it outside the VPC with no cluster. Status is preview because the only page that states a status says public preview.
sources: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/cs/user-guide/agent-sandbox/ (read 2026-10-31; updated 2026-06-23; states public preview and no GPU)

entry.name: PAI-Instant Service
entry.purpose: PAI's E2B-compatible MicroVM sandboxes for RL training and evaluation; China regions only.
entry.avoidWhen: International designs; use acs-agent-sandbox or agent-sandbox.
entry.note: Documented on the international help site, but its page lists only China East 2 (Shanghai), China North 6 (Ulanqab) and China Northwest 2 (Zhongwei). Lifecycle stage not stated.

catalog.rationale: A guard entry. The docs describe exactly the user's 'sandboxes for model training' case, so a search or a customer may name it. With an entry, 'PAI Sandbox' resolves, the row carries the china-only flag, and the validator warns instead of the model guessing.

entry.name: PAI-LangStudio
entry.purpose: PAI's builder for LLM application and RAG flows; retires on 2027-03-09.
entry.avoidWhen: Any new design; it retires on 2027-03-09.
entry.note: Retires 2027-03-09 16:00. Its named successor, Model Studio application development, supports only China (Beijing) and is closed to new international accounts. For new builds use a PAI-EAS RAG or Dify service, AgentCore or Dify on ACK.

catalog.rationale: Older PAI tutorials and the model's memory recommend LangStudio for RAG. As a legacy entry with a successor it costs no prompt row: resolve() switches a 'LangStudio' node to pai-eas with a retired-product warning that carries the date. pai-eas is our judgment for the successor (the RAG and Dify scenario templates are its PAI-native replacements); the official successor is unusable internationally.

entry.purpose: Alibaba's AI platform umbrella; prefer its stage entries: pai-dsw, pai-dlc, pai-eas, pai-model-gallery.
entry.useWhen: A generic mention of PAI before the stage is known, or Designer low-code ML.
entry.avoidWhen: Any design that shows a specific stage (use pai-dsw, pai-dlc, pai-eas); hosted Qwen calls (use Model Studio).
entry.note: Designer (low-code ML on MaxCompute) stays under this entry. PAI-Studio 1.0 is retired in every region (last phase 2026-09-30). iTAG is China-only and closed to new PAI customers since 2026-08-01.

catalog.rationale: Keep a thin umbrella so 'use PAI' and older diagrams still resolve. Move the module aliases (EAS, PAI-EAS, pai_eas, PAI-DSW, PAI-DLC, Model Gallery) to the stage entries, because an alias may name only one id.

entry.name: Agent Sandbox (Flash Edition)
entry.purpose: Managed E2B-compatible sandboxes for agent code, browser and desktop tasks, created by API; no cluster.
entry.useWhen: Agents running untrusted code or browsers, teams moving from E2B, or teams that want no cluster to run.
entry.avoidWhen: The user wants sandboxes on ACS or Kubernetes (use acs-agent-sandbox), or GPU work.
entry.note: Same service the Function Compute docs call FC Agent Sandbox (inferred; Flash needs Function Compute). No lifecycle stage stated, and independent billing is an invite-only preview. The Desktop template must be built once; snapshots and AgenticFS volumes are invite-only. Container Edition on ACS is acs-agent-sandbox.
intents: sandbox for an agent to run code or browse

catalog.rationale: Split the two editions so each lands in the right container. This entry becomes the managed Flash Edition (region scope, outside the VPC) and the default for a generic 'agent sandbox'. Status moves from ga to preview: no page states GA, and the FC billing page calls independent billing an invite-only preview. Express, Speed and Flash all stay as aliases because the docs still use all three.

entry.useWhen: Kubernetes workloads without node management, bursty jobs, or hosting agent sandboxes.
entry.note: Recommended successor for ACK Serverless clusters. GPU pods (gpu and gpu-hpn compute classes) are an invitational preview: confirm access with the account team. Agent Sandbox pods have no GPU; draw them as acs-agent-sandbox.

catalog.rationale: ACS hosts both GPU pods and the Container Edition sandbox. Pairing it with acs-agent-sandbox lets the model find the new entry, and the note stops anyone from putting training inside a sandbox.

entry.avoidWhen: Regions other than Singapore (the only international region), or no allowlist access yet; use pai-dlc on GPUs.
entry.note: Allowlist access, requested by support ticket or your account manager. Subscription is the standard path; pay-as-you-go is a further allowlisted option. Backs PAI DSW, DLC and EAS quotas. ACK Lingjun cluster creation ends December 2026; use ACK Pro Lingjun.

catalog.rationale: The fact-check found the allowlist applies to Lingjun access as a whole, not only to pay-as-you-go, so 'pay-as-you-go by allowlist only' understates it. The avoidWhen line puts the Singapore-only fact where the model can see it, which matters for EU or Japan training designs.

entry.note: ECS GPU instance families; draw as an ECS node with a GPU marker. Newer families (gn8v, gn8is, gn9 and ebmgn9) are limited to select regions or invitation, and no page states Singapore stock: check the console.

catalog.rationale: Point the alternatives at the PAI stages instead of the umbrella, and stop diagrams from implying that every GPU family is self-serve in Singapore.

entry.avoidWhen: Coding-tool subscriptions; use Coding Plan or Token Plan. Self-hosted or custom weights; use PAI-EAS.
entry.note: Keys and model lists are per region. Agent apps and knowledge base are closed to new international accounts (see model-studio-apps). Fine-tuning and batch exist only in Singapore among international regions; Singapore fine-tuning is SFT on a few Qwen models, and tuned models cannot be exported. PrivateLink is documented for Beijing and Hong Kong only, not Singapore.
intents: call Qwen or other LLM APIs from our app
light SFT of a Qwen model without managing GPUs

catalog.rationale: Gives the model the managed-versus-PAI boundary for post-training and the Singapore private-access gap, which changes RAG network drawings (NAT egress instead of a PrivateLink badge).

entry.note: Sits between the app and its models; part of the API Gateway family. A vLLM or SGLang service on PAI-EAS is fronted as a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible backend; EAS is not a named service type.

catalog.rationale: Replace the umbrella id with pai-eas, the node AI Gateway actually fronts. The note records that this pairing is an inference: the gateway documents self-hosted vLLM and SGLang, and EAS LLM endpoints are OpenAI-compatible.
Replace the umbrella with the training stage that mounts CPFS.
sources: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/pai/use-cases/qwen3-reinforcement-learning-best-practices (read 2026-10-31; CPFS or NAS dataset mount on DLC)

entry.avoidWhen: Traces that must stay in Singapore or the EU: it runs only in Hong Kong internationally; use SLS or ARMS.

catalog.rationale: The region limit is only in the note, which the model never sees. A residency-pinned AI design that adds 'evaluation and tracing' would otherwise draw a cross-region AgentLoop.

entry.note: Singapore is the only international endpoint (endpoint list, 2026-08-22). Runs on Function Compute; AgentRun is listed for PrivateLink. The memory store is Tablestore (RDS memory is in maintenance mode). Its built-in sandbox has an optional upgrade path to FC Cloud Sandbox (agent-sandbox), with no retirement date.

catalog.rationale: AgentRun reaches the customer VPC and is on the PrivateLink list, so it may sit VPC-attached. Tablestore is the documented memory backend, and the sandbox upgrade path ties it to agent-sandbox.

entry.useWhen: Agents that must drive Windows or Android environments, browse, or operate desktops safely.
entry.note: A separate product from Agent Sandbox; SDK endpoints in Singapore and Shanghai. Covers Windows and Android runtimes. A guide (2026-10-27) moves Linux desktop automation to Agent Sandbox's Desktop template; no deprecation is announced.

catalog.rationale: Keeps AgentBay distinct from the two Agent Sandbox editions and gives it the job only it does: Windows and Android environments.

entry.note: The documented memory store for AgentRun, and a knowledge-base connector for AgentCore.

catalog.rationale: Lets the managed agent pattern find its memory store.

entry.note: Renamed from Multi-agent Governance and Collaboration Platform (AgentTeams) on 2026-08-28; billed since 2026-09-18; activate the service before first use. Knowledge-base connectors are Tablestore and the Model Studio knowledge base (Beijing only per the earlier review). Not Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

catalog.rationale: In Singapore the working knowledge-base path for AgentCore is Tablestore.
sources: research/findings/5-ai-dev-products.md F8 (Bailian connector Beijing-only, from the AgentCore llms.txt index)

entry.purpose: Managed vector search API (Proxima engine); paid clusters bill per instance-hour.
entry.avoidWhen: Designs that need documented private VPC access; use Milvus.
entry.note: Singapore and Virginia. The free trial cluster is for testing and is released after 30 days. The docs describe no VPC access.

catalog.rationale: The current purpose ('fully serverless') holds only for the free trial. Paid clusters bill per instance-hour, and no VPC path is documented, which matters for private RAG.

entry.note: The managed knowledge-base feature in the Milvus tutorials lists mainland China regions only: internationally, use Milvus as a plain vector store with your own ingestion. The PAI-EAS RAG template does not offer Milvus as a built-in store.

catalog.rationale: Stops the app from promising the console knowledge-base workflow to a Singapore customer, or wiring Milvus into the EAS RAG template.

entry.note: Vector Search edition in Singapore and Frankfurt; LLM-based conversational search edition in Singapore. AI Search Open Platform services (parsing, chunking, rerank) are documented for Shanghai and Frankfurt only. A PAI-EAS RAG service reaches OpenSearch over the public network only.

catalog.rationale: Two region and network facts that change Singapore RAG drawings.

entry.note: Model Studio private endpoints are documented for Beijing and Hong Kong only, not Singapore. AI services on the list include PAI EAS, Milvus, AgentRun and OSS; Tablestore, Tair and AI Gateway are not listed.

catalog.rationale: So a 'private RAG in Singapore' diagram does not draw a PrivateLink badge to Model Studio.

entry.note: New in 2026; supports OIDC and on-behalf-of access. ACS Agent Sandbox uses it for OSS mounts and egress credential injection. Regions and billing were not confirmed in this review: check Singapore before proposing it.

catalog.rationale: It is the documented credential path for Container Edition sandboxes, but its availability field 'intl' is an assumption nobody verified.
sources: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/cs/llms.txt (read 2026-10-31; index lists the OSS mount with Agent Identity page)

entry.note: Dify can also run as one PAI-EAS service backed by RDS PostgreSQL, Tair (Redis), Elasticsearch and OSS in the same VPC; their VPCs cannot change after creation. Dify's own code sandbox container is not an agent sandbox product.

catalog.rationale: EAS-hosted Dify is the second documented Dify path and a practical LangStudio replacement.

notAdded.why: InferX lists no regions, availability or allowlist. Token Service is in Beijing, Singapore, Frankfurt and Tokyo, but its relationship to Model Studio is unexplained, and it prices qwen3.8-max differently ($2.40/$7.20 vs $2/$6 per 1M in Singapore). An entry now would split 'call Qwen by API' across two products. Revisit when the relationship is documented.
Managed SFT and dedicated deployment are still the Model Studio endpoint, so a second box would duplicate model-studio. Captured in the model-studio note and prompt rule R19 instead.
Not re-verified by the fact-checks, and it is an add-on rather than a drawable hop; ack's purpose already mentions its AI suite.
Singapore is supported, but 'same product as LLM Intelligent Q&A Edition' is only inferred, and the edition already resolves as an alias of opensearch. Low value for the requested patterns.
Free public beta with no SLA, no stated regions, and cached data cleared when the beta ends.

The ALB dedicated gateway is the existing alb node; the shared gateway is implicit; the managed dedicated gateway is an edge label. Designer stays under the pai umbrella. iTAG is China-only and closed to new customers.

patterns.name: Training sandboxes for people (isolated data-science workspaces)
patterns.evidence: documented parts, composed by us: DSW and DLC features are documented; the isolation story (workspace, VPC, RAM role, NAT-only egress) is our design.
triggers: GPU notebooks to train or fine-tune models
each researcher gets a GPU workspace
patterns.placement: pai-dsw and pai-dlc are region scope and sit on the AI shelf; nas, cpfs and nat need a VPC group in the region (nat on its boundary). ram and actiontrail go to the account band. Say where the isolation comes from: per-person instances, workspace quotas, the VPC, NAT-only egress and RAM roles. DSW documents nothing stronger, so do not call it a hardened multi-tenant sandbox.
mistakes: Drawing an agent sandbox (acs-agent-sandbox, agent-sandbox, agentbay) for people who train models.
Drawing the pai umbrella, or one box for notebooks, training and serving.
AccessKeys in notebooks instead of a RAM role with STS credentials.
Using DSW to host a production model; that is pai-eas.
Promising Lingjun without the allowlist, or outside Singapore.

patterns.name: Post-training on PAI, then serving on PAI-EAS
patterns.evidence: documented: Model Gallery runs SFT and DPO on DLC and deploys to EAS; the ChatLearn GRPO and Megatron walkthroughs go DSW -> DLC -> EAS (both recommend or require China (Ulanqab)).
triggers: fine-tune Qwen on our data and host it
train our own model then deploy it
variants: No-code: pai-model-gallery -> pai-dlc (SFT or DPO, full, LoRA or QLoRA) -> oss -> pai-eas.
Custom or RL: pai-dsw (single-node debug) -> pai-dlc on lingjun with cpfs or nas -> pai-eas (vLLM).
Managed: model-studio only, for light SFT of a supported Qwen model in Singapore; no weight export, and dedicated deployment is billed separately.
patterns.placement: All PAI stages sit on the AI shelf; draw only one deploy edge (from the gallery when it is used, else from pai-dlc). The consumer app and AI Gateway sit in the VPC and call pai-eas with an edge labelled 'private endpoint' or 'VPC direct'.
mistakes: One pai node standing for both training and serving, or no deploy edge.
Model Studio fine-tuning when the customer needs DPO, RL, another base model or weights they keep: in Singapore it is SFT only, with no export.
Presenting GRPO as a general Model Gallery feature; it is documented only for Qwen3 32B and smaller in the Qwen3 guide.
Promising pay-as-you-go Lingjun, or Lingjun outside Singapore.
Exposing the tuned model on a public endpoint with no gateway, quota or guardrails.

patterns.name: Self-hosted LLM inference at scale on PAI-EAS
patterns.evidence: documented: EAS LLM deployment (vLLM, SGLang, BladeLLM, OpenAI-compatible), autoscaling, resource types, gateways and the MoE template with prefill, decode and router sub-services. AI Gateway in front of EAS is inferred.
triggers: token quotas per team on our own GPUs
patterns.placement: pai-eas sits on the AI shelf; the app and AI Gateway sit in the VPC. Scaling, the LLM router and prefill-decode separation are EAS features: put them in the why text, never as extra nodes or an ess node. Spiky traffic: a dedicated group as the baseline with public overflow (virtual resource group or elastic pool). Very large models: a Lingjun quota (allowlist).
mistakes: Apps calling the EAS endpoint directly with no gateway, quota or guardrails.
Scale to zero together with a dedicated gateway (not allowed), or no warning about the cold start.
An ess (Auto Scaling) node or a separate router node.
Saying AI Gateway lists EAS as a built-in service type; it is fronted as a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible backend.
Assuming per-request billing: EAS bills for as long as resources are held, even when a service fails to start.
VPC direct, NLB or Nacos access without security group rules: that traffic is subject to them.

patterns.name: RAG on PAI-EAS with a self-hosted model
patterns.evidence: documented: the PAI-EAS RAG scenario (PAI-RAG) with LLM-decoupled or integrated modes and its listed vector stores.
triggers: RAG chatbot with our own model
documents must stay with self-hosted weights
patterns.placement: Both pai-eas nodes sit on the AI shelf; elasticsearch or rds sit in the VPC, hologres on the shelf. Services and the vector store share one VPC for private access. Use LLM-decoupled mode for anything but small models. If the LLM is a Model Studio model instead of llm-svc, the RAG service needs NAT with SNAT.
mistakes: Model Studio knowledge base or app builder: closed to new international accounts.
PAI-LangStudio: retires on 2027-03-09.
Milvus as the template's vector store (not offered), or FAISS in production (quick start only).
OpenSearch drawn as a private in-VPC store for this service; it is reached over the public network only.
Copying the Beijing Model Studio endpoint from the guide; use the Singapore key and endpoint.
Calling PAI-RAG's code sandbox an ACS sandbox; it uses Function Compute (AgentRun) sandboxes only.

patterns.name: RAG on Model Studio APIs, built from parts
patterns.evidence: composed by us: Model Studio embedding, rerank and generation plus a vector store are documented; the ingestion worker (OSS -> FC -> embed -> Milvus) has no official reference architecture.
triggers: chatbot on our documents with Qwen
knowledge base Q&A for a new international account
patterns.placement: milvus and the app sit in the VPC; model-studio, oss and fc sit on the shelf. Model Studio has no documented private endpoint in Singapore, so VPC compute reaches it through NAT (draw nat when the egress path matters). Use the Batch API (Singapore) for bulk re-embedding. Do not hard-code model ids in labels.
mistakes: Model Studio knowledge base, app builder or the Responses file_search tool (all depend on the restricted application features).
The Milvus console knowledge-base workflow (mainland regions only).
AI Search Open Platform parsing in a Singapore design (Shanghai and Frankfurt only).
A PrivateLink badge to Model Studio in Singapore.
DashVector when the design needs a documented private VPC path.
Embedding model, vector store and app in different regions.

patterns.name: Agent hosting with ACS sandboxes for code and browser tools
patterns.evidence: documented parts: Container Edition components, E2B flow, egress control and hibernation; the Kimi case (official Container Service blog) runs agents on ACK and ACS Agent Sandbox at scale. The full composition is ours.
triggers: host AI agents for our customers
agents must run generated code safely
E2B alternative on our own cluster
variants: Agent uses sandbox: the agent runs in the acs app tier and calls sandboxes as its tool layer (shown above).
Agent in sandbox: each user's long-lived agent (for example OpenClaw) lives in its own sandbox; idle ones hibernate.
No Kubernetes: see agent-hosting-managed (agentrun with agent-sandbox).
patterns.placement: acs and acs-agent-sandbox both sit in the VPC; the sandbox is an ordinary node with an edge from acs, never an attachment. The sandbox-manager E2B endpoint sits behind an Ingress (ALB) with an API key; users reach the agent API, never the sandboxes. Egress goes through the cluster egress gateway with L7 allowlist rules; credentials are injected there, so sandboxes hold no long-term keys.
mistakes: GPU work inside a sandbox: Agent Sandbox pods are CPU and memory only.
Sandboxes reachable straight from the internet, or with open internet egress.
Presenting Agent Sandbox as GA: the ACS page says public preview.
Using pai-instant (China-only) or calling PAI-RAG's code sandbox or Dify's sandbox container an ACS sandbox.
Expecting hibernation to keep WebSocket, SSE or gRPC connections; clients must reconnect.
Taking '15,000 sandboxes per minute' as a design number; the default creation quota is burst 100, then 20 per minute.
Adding AgentLoop to a Singapore design without flagging that traces go to Hong Kong.

patterns.name: Sandbox fleet for agentic RL and evaluation rollouts
patterns.evidence: Variant A is documented (VeRL on ACK with KubeRay, a Lingjun GPU node, sandbox-manager and a SandboxSet warm pool behind ALB Ingress, OSS); whether those sandboxes run on ACS compute is not stated on the page. Variant B (a PAI-DLC trainer driving ACS sandboxes) is our proposed design: no page connects DLC or EAS to Agent Sandbox.
variants: A documented: ack (KubeRay and VeRL on a Lingjun GPU node, sandbox-manager behind ALB Ingress) -> acs-agent-sandbox warm pool; data and checkpoints in oss.
B proposed: pai-dlc trainer (Lingjun quota, cpfs) -> acs-agent-sandbox in an acs cluster in the same VPC; final policy served on pai-eas. Say it is a proposed design.
patterns.placement: The trainer (pai-dlc on the shelf, or ack in the VPC) and the acs cluster must share a VPC or be connected; acs and acs-agent-sandbox sit in the VPC. GPUs stay with the trainer; sandboxes run the environments and tools.
mistakes: pai-instant: built for this, but China regions only.
Training or policy inference inside the sandboxes (no GPU).
Presenting variant B as an Alibaba reference architecture.
Planning a large fleet on the default creation quota; request an increase first.
Lingjun outside Singapore or without allowlist access.
Rollout sandboxes with open internet egress.

patterns.name: Managed agent hosting without Kubernetes (AgentRun and Flash sandboxes)
patterns.evidence: documented parts: AgentRun runtime and Tablestore memory in Singapore; Agent Sandbox Flash Edition in Singapore. The composition is ours.
triggers: host our LangChain agent without servers
agent with memory, tools and tracing
patterns.placement: agentrun, agent-sandbox, model-studio and tablestore all sit on the region shelf; there is no cluster. A VPC appears only when the agent must reach private databases (AgentRun VPC access).
mistakes: RDS as the AgentRun memory store (in maintenance mode); use Tablestore.
Sandboxes drawn as plain Function Compute functions.
AgentLoop in a Singapore- or EU-pinned design (Hong Kong only).

promptRules.placement: Append after R18 under a new heading '# AI designs'. Rules only mention ids, never prices or figures (R16).
rules: R19 PAI is drawn as its stages: pai-dsw (notebooks for people), pai-dlc (training and fine-tuning jobs), pai-eas (serving models, RAG services and agent apps) and pai-model-gallery (no-code fine-tune and deploy; it starts DLC jobs and EAS services and has no compute). Use pai only for a generic mention, never two pai nodes. Train then serve: pai-dlc -> oss (checkpoints) and one deploy edge to pai-eas (kind control). Self-hosted or tuned weights go on pai-eas; hosted Qwen calls go to model-studio. Light SFT of a supported Qwen model without GPUs is model-studio (Singapore, no weight export); DPO, RL, other models or weights the customer keeps are PAI. Large training is pai-dlc on lingjun with cpfs; Lingjun needs allowlist access and its only international region is Singapore: say so. pai-eas sits on the region shelf: draw private access as an edge labelled "private endpoint" or "VPC direct", and add nat when EAS calls Model Studio or the internet.

R20 Sandbox means two things; say which you drew. People who develop or train models: pai-dsw, with pai-dlc for bigger jobs, never an agent sandbox. Isolated execution of agent-written code, browsers or RL rollouts: acs-agent-sandbox when the user says ACS, Kubernetes, many tenants or RL rollouts (draw the acs node too, with an edge acs -> acs-agent-sandbox); otherwise agent-sandbox (managed E2B API, no cluster); agentbay for Windows or Android. No sandbox has GPUs: training and models stay on pai-dlc, pai-eas, lingjun or egs. Both sandbox entries are preview: say so once. A pai-dlc trainer driving ACS sandboxes is a proposed design, not an Alibaba reference: say so. pai-instant is China-only.

R21 RAG on a self-hosted model: the PAI-EAS RAG service and the LLM are two pai-eas nodes, the vector store is elasticsearch, hologres or rds in the same VPC (milvus is not in that template; FAISS is for demos), and files are in oss. RAG on hosted models follows R14. Model Studio has no documented private endpoint in Singapore: VPC compute reaches it through nat.

Ship R19-R21 first and run the new eval cases; add this example only if structural failures remain (two pai nodes, a missing deploy edge, a sandbox outside the VPC). It costs about the tokens shown in meta.measured.workedExampleTokens, on top of a prompt already over budget.

case.title: Training sandboxes for data scientists (DSW, not an agent sandbox)
case.reference: PAI-DSW workspaces for each data scientist with OSS and NAS (or CPFS) mounts, PAI-DLC for bigger fine-tuning jobs, a VPC with NAT for package installs and a RAM role instead of keys, in Singapore. No agent sandbox (ACS Agent Sandbox, Agent Sandbox, AgentBay or PAI-Instant), and no single PAI box.

turns.ask: Our 12 data scientists need sandbox environments with GPUs where they can experiment with and fine-tune models on our datasets. We are in Singapore.

case.title: Agent hosting with ACS sandboxes
case.reference: Users reach an agent API on ACS (behind an ALB); the ACS cluster claims sandboxes from ACS Agent Sandbox (Container Edition) for the generated code, drawn inside the VPC with an edge from the ACS node; the agent calls Qwen through AI Gateway and Model Studio (or a PAI-EAS model); sandbox egress is allowlisted through NAT; credentials through Agent Identity or KMS. Says the sandbox is in preview and has no GPU. No PAI-Instant Service.

turns.ask: A client wants to host AI agents for their own customers. Each agent writes and runs Python code, which must execute in isolated sandboxes on ACS. The agents use Qwen models.

case.title: Post-training on PAI, then serving on PAI-EAS
case.reference: Training data in OSS; SFT through PAI Model Gallery or a PAI-DLC job; checkpoints back to OSS; a deploy edge to PAI-EAS (vLLM) serving a private endpoint, ideally behind AI Gateway. Separate stage nodes, not one PAI box. No LangStudio.

turns.ask: We want to fine-tune Qwen3-8B on our support tickets with SFT and then serve it privately for our internal apps. Use PAI.

case.title: RAG on PAI-EAS with a self-hosted LLM
case.reference: An ALB in front of a PAI-EAS RAG service and a separate PAI-EAS LLM service (decoupled mode); vector store Elasticsearch, Hologres or RDS PostgreSQL in the same VPC; knowledge files in OSS. No Milvus in the template, no FAISS in production, no Model Studio knowledge base and no LangStudio.

turns.ask: Build a RAG chatbot over our product manuals using the PAI-EAS RAG deployment with our own self-hosted LLM, in Singapore.

case.title: RAG on Model Studio APIs without GPUs
case.reference: Compute (Function Compute, SAE, ACS or AgentRun) calls Model Studio for embedding, rerank and generation, retrieves from Milvus or OpenSearch, keeps documents in OSS and has an ingestion step; AI Gateway and AI Guardrails are good additions; NAT egress from VPC compute because Singapore has no documented Model Studio private endpoint. No Model Studio knowledge base and no self-hosted model.

turns.ask: We want a RAG assistant over our help-center articles that uses Qwen through Model Studio. We don't want to manage GPUs or host models ourselves.

case.title: Self-hosted LLM inference at scale with per-team quotas
case.reference: AI Gateway (token quotas per consumer, fallback) in front of a PAI-EAS LLM service (vLLM or SGLang) with weights in OSS; autoscaling and router or prefill-decode separation described in the why text, not as extra nodes; a Lingjun quota optional for very large models with the allowlist caveat; optional Model Studio fallback and AI Guardrails. No Auto Scaling node and no single PAI box.

turns.ask: We want to self-host a large Qwen model for about 2,000 concurrent internal users in Singapore, with per-team token quotas and failover.

case.title: Training data stays in Singapore; evaluation added later
case.reference: Turn 1 pins Singapore and draws PAI-DLC or Model Gallery training with OSS and PAI-EAS serving, all in Singapore. Turn 2 adds tracing and evaluation with in-region SLS or ARMS (or Model Studio as a judge), not AgentLoop, which runs only in Hong Kong internationally; if it mentions AgentLoop it says why it is left out.

turns.ask: Our training data must stay in Singapore. We want to post-train an open Qwen model on PAI and serve it to our app.
Add tracing and quality evaluation for the model's answers.

case.title: EU-only training data and large distributed training (no Lingjun in Frankfurt)
case.reference: Everything in Frankfurt: PAI-DLC on general GPU resources (or GPU ECS or ACK) with OSS and NAS or CPFS, and PAI-EAS (or Kubernetes) for serving. Says Lingjun is not offered in Frankfurt (Singapore is its only international region), so it is left out. No other region.

turns.ask: We are a German company and our training data must stay in Frankfurt. We want to train a 30B model across many GPUs with fast shared storage, then serve it.
